title: Dividing by ten with a magic number
description:
Write unsigned division and remainder by 10 with a multiply by `0xCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCD` and a shift, no `div`:

| Function | Returns |
|---|---|
| `udiv10(x)` | `x / 10` for an unsigned 64-bit `x` |
| `umod10(x)` | `x % 10` |
| `digit_count(x)` | how many decimal digits `x` has (1 for 0), using your division |

starter.solution.asm:
udiv10:
        mov     rax, rdi
        shr     rax, 3
        ret

umod10:
        mov     rax, rdi
        and     rax, 7
        ret

digit_count:
        mov     eax, 1
        ret

solution.solution.asm:
udiv10:
        mov     rax, 0xCCCCCCCCCCCCCCCD
        mul     rdi
        mov     rax, rdx
        shr     rax, 3
        ret

umod10:
        mov     rcx, rdi
        call    udiv10
        lea     rax, [rax + rax*4]
        add     rax, rax
        sub     rcx, rax
        mov     rax, rcx
        ret

digit_count:
        mov     r8d, 1
.loop:  cmp     rdi, 10
        jb      .done
        call    udiv10
        mov     rdi, rax
        inc     r8
        jmp     .loop
.done:  mov     rax, r8
        ret

hints: `mul rdi` with the magic number in `rax` leaves the high 64 bits of the product in `rdx`; three more bits of shift give the quotient (lesson 8.02).
The remainder is `x − (x / 10) × 10`, and `× 10` is `lea` plus `add`. Save `x` in a scratch register before calling `udiv10`, since `mul` changes `rdx`.
rules: Do not use div or idiv.
unitTests:
test "divide"
    udiv10(1234567) == 123456
    udiv10(9) == 0
    udiv10(10) == 1
    udiv10(-1) == 1844674407370955161
test "remainder"
    umod10(1234567) == 7
    umod10(10) == 0
    umod10(-1) == 5
test "digits"
    digit_count(0) == 1
    digit_count(9) == 1
    digit_count(10) == 2
    digit_count(1000000) == 7
    digit_count(-1) == 20
